per_query.original_query: When should an antimalarial medicine recommended in a national treatment policy be changed due to treatment failure?
gold_reference_texts: An antimalarial medicine recommended in national policy should be changed if the total treatment failure proportion is ≥ 10% in vivo.

per_query.original_query: What average cure rate in clinical trials is required to introduce a new antimalarial medicine into national treatment policy?
gold_reference_texts: Introducing a new antimalarial medicine into national treatment policy requires an average cure rate of > 95% in clinical trials.

per_query.original_query: What formulation of paediatric antimalarial drugs is preferred for young children and infants?
gold_reference_texts: Solid paediatric formulations such as dispersible tablets are preferred over liquid formulations for young children and infants.

per_query.original_query: Is mass testing and treatment (MTaT) recommended to reduce malaria transmission?
gold_reference_texts: Mass testing and treatment (MTaT) to reduce malaria transmission is not recommended.

per_query.original_query: Who can receive targeted drug administration (TDA) as chemoprevention in very low to low transmission settings?
gold_reference_texts: Targeted drug administration can be given to individuals with an increased risk of infection compared to the general population.

per_query.original_query: Is routine malaria testing and treatment recommended for individuals arriving at points of entry?
gold_reference_texts: Routine malaria testing and treatment at points of entry to reduce importation is not recommended.

per_query.original_query: Who should be given antimalarial medicine as chemoprevention in reactive drug administration (RDA)?
gold_reference_texts: Reactive drug administration is provided to individuals living with or near a confirmed case, as well as those sharing the same infection risk such as co-workers and co-travellers.

per_query.original_query: Where should reactive indoor residual spraying (IRS) be conducted following a confirmed malaria case?
gold_reference_texts: Reactive indoor residual spraying of insecticide can be conducted in the houses of confirmed cases and their neighbours.

per_query.original_query: What does the medical abbreviation AL stand for in the WHO malaria guidelines?
gold_reference_texts: AL stands for artemether-lumefantrine.

per_query.original_query: What does the abbreviation IPTp stand for?
gold_reference_texts: IPTp stands for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy.

per_query.original_query: What is the full meaning of the abbreviation SMC in malaria interventions?
gold_reference_texts: SMC stands for seasonal malaria chemoprevention.

per_query.original_query: How many estimated global cases and deaths from malaria occurred in 2023 according to the World malaria report?
gold_reference_texts: In 2023, there were an estimated 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths from malaria globally.

per_query.original_query: What is the 2030 Global Technical Strategy target for reducing malaria mortality rates compared to 2015?
gold_reference_texts: The target for reducing global malaria mortality rates by 2030 compared with 2015 is at least 90%.

per_query.original_query: How many countries is the Global Technical Strategy targeting for malaria elimination by 2025?
gold_reference_texts: The target for 2025 is to eliminate malaria from at least 20 countries in which malaria was transmitted in 2015.

per_query.original_query: Which Plasmodium species commonly infect humans, and which is considered the most dangerous?
gold_reference_texts: Plasmodium falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, and P. ovale most commonly infect humans.
Plasmodium falciparum is the most dangerous species.

per_query.original_query: How long does the malaria parasite typically take to develop inside a mosquito into an infective form for humans?
gold_reference_texts: The malaria parasite generally requires 7 to 10 days to develop inside the mosquito into a form infective to humans.

per_query.original_query: What annual parasite incidence and P. falciparum prevalence define high malaria transmission areas?
gold_reference_texts: High transmission areas have an annual parasite incidence of ≥ 450 cases per 1000 population.
High transmission areas have a Plasmodium falciparum prevalence rate of ≥ 35%.

per_query.original_query: What is the annual parasite incidence range for areas categorized as having low malaria transmission?
gold_reference_texts: Low transmission areas have an annual parasite incidence of 100–250 cases per 1000 population.

per_query.original_query: Which two vector control interventions are recommended by WHO for large-scale deployment?
gold_reference_texts: WHO-prequalified ITNs and WHO-prequalified indoor residual spraying (IRS) are the vector control interventions recommended for large-scale deployment.

per_query.original_query: Approximately how many Anopheles species are major vector species for malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Out of more than 400 Anopheles species, around 40 are major malaria vectors.

per_query.original_query: What factors attract female Anopheles mosquitoes to a human host?
gold_reference_texts: Female mosquitoes are attracted to hosts by exhaled carbon dioxide, lactic acid, host odours, warmth, and moisture.

per_query.original_query: What percentage of clinical cases averted in Africa between 2000 and 2015 was attributed to ITNs?
gold_reference_texts: Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) made the largest contribution by averting 68% of clinical malaria cases in Africa between 2000 and 2015.

per_query.original_query: What percentage of reporting malaria-endemic sites detected pyrethroid resistance in at least one vector species?
gold_reference_texts: Globally, resistance to pyrethroids was detected in at least one malaria vector in 68% of monitored sites.

per_query.original_query: Why should vector control programmes avoid switching between different pyrethroid insecticides to manage resistance?
gold_reference_texts: Differences in adult mosquito mortality assays do not reflect operationally relevant performance differences among commonly used pyrethroids.

per_query.original_query: What are insecticide mixtures in vector control?
gold_reference_texts: Mixtures are co-formulations combining two or more insecticides with different modes of action.

per_query.original_query: How is residual malaria transmission defined?
gold_reference_texts: Residual transmission refers to ongoing malaria transmission that persists despite the wide implementation of an effective malaria programme.

per_query.original_query: How should old insecticide-treated nets be disposed of according to WHO guidelines?
gold_reference_texts: WHO recommends burying old nets in non-permeable soil away from water sources instead of open-air burning.

per_query.original_query: By what rate ratio do ITNs reduce all-cause child mortality compared to no nets?
gold_reference_texts: ITNs reduce all-cause child mortality with a rate ratio of 0.83 compared to no nets.

per_query.original_query: How does piperonyl butoxide (PBO) work in pyrethroid-PBO nets to enhance efficacy against resistant mosquitoes?
gold_reference_texts: Piperonyl butoxide (PBO) inhibits metabolic enzymes, primarily oxidases, preventing mosquitoes from detoxifying pyrethroids.

per_query.original_query: What type of recommendation has WHO issued for deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs instead of pyrethroid-only LLINs in areas with pyrethroid resistance?
gold_reference_texts: WHO provides a strong recommendation for deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs instead of pyrethroid-only LLINs in pyrethroid-resistant areas based on moderate certainty evidence.

per_query.original_query: What proportion of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs were reported as torn two years after deployment in trial data from Tanzania?
gold_reference_texts: 34% of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs were torn (hole area ≥ 790 cm²) two years after deployment in the trial.

per_query.original_query: How does chlorfenapyr exert its insecticidal effect on mosquitoes?
gold_reference_texts: Chlorfenapyr disrupts ATP production in mosquito mitochondria, leading to cell dysfunction and death.

per_query.original_query: By what percentage was clinical malaria incidence reduced two years after deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs compared to pyrethroid-only LLINs?
gold_reference_texts: Clinical malaria incidence was reduced by approximately 40% two years post-deployment of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs compared to pyrethroid-only LLINs.

per_query.original_query: Is pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITN recommended over pyrethroid-PBO ITN for malaria prevention in pyrethroid-resistant areas?
gold_reference_texts: Pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITNs are conditionally recommended against deployment over pyrethroid-PBO ITNs in pyrethroid-resistant areas.

per_query.original_query: What average willingness-to-pay for spatial emanators was reported in Cambodian studies?
gold_reference_texts: The average willingness-to-pay for spatial emanators reported in Cambodian studies was US$ 0.30 per unit.

per_query.original_query: What percentage of study participants in China reported consistent use of mosquito coils?
gold_reference_texts: Over 94% of participants in a study conducted in China consistently used mosquito coils.

per_query.original_query: Is space spraying recommended for the prevention and control of malaria in areas with ongoing transmission?
gold_reference_texts: Space spraying is conditionally recommended against for malaria prevention in areas with ongoing transmission.

per_query.original_query: By what rate ratio does house screening reduce clinical malaria incidence caused by P. falciparum in trial evidence?
gold_reference_texts: House screening reduces clinical P. falciparum malaria incidence with a rate ratio of 0.38.

per_query.original_query: What additional animals were reported to have reduced entry into houses following screening in the Gambian study?
gold_reference_texts: In the Gambian study, house screening reduced entry of bats, cockroaches, earwigs, geckos, mice, rats, snakes, and toads.

per_query.original_query: How are causal prophylaxis and suppressive prophylaxis distinguished for malaria prevention in travellers?
gold_reference_texts: Causal prophylaxis inhibits liver-stage development, while suppressive prophylaxis kills asexual blood-stage parasites.

per_query.original_query: When should intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy (IPTp-SP) be initiated?
gold_reference_texts: IPTp-SP administration should begin in the second trimester, starting as early as possible after 13 weeks of pregnancy.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended dosage and tablet composition for IPTp-SP administered as directly observed therapy?
gold_reference_texts: IPTp-SP is given as three tablets containing 500 mg/25 mg SP each, totaling 1500 mg/75 mg SP.

per_query.original_query: Why should IPTp-SP not be administered before week 13 of pregnancy?
gold_reference_texts: IPTp-SP is contraindicated prior to week 13 of pregnancy because of the risk of fetal malformation.

per_query.original_query: Why should high doses of folic acid be avoided during IPTp-SP administration?
gold_reference_texts: Daily doses of folic acid of 5 mg or more counteract the antimalarial efficacy of SP.

per_query.original_query: By how much does IPTp-SP increase mean birthweight in babies born to women of all gravidae?
gold_reference_texts: IPTp-SP increases mean birthweight by an average of 57 grams across all gravidae compared to no IPTp-SP.

per_query.original_query: What threshold of parasite prevalence or annual parasite incidence defines moderate to high perennial malaria transmission settings for PMC?
gold_reference_texts: Moderate to high perennial transmission settings are defined as having P. falciparum parasite prevalence > 10% or API > 250 per 1000 population.

per_query.original_query: What minimum interval should be maintained between doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in PMC schedules?
gold_reference_texts: Doses of SP in perennial malaria chemoprevention must be administered at least one month apart.

per_query.original_query: What drug combination is widely recommended and used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) in African children?
gold_reference_texts: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SP+AQ) is the drug combination widely used for SMC.

per_query.original_query: By what proportion does SMC reduce the risk of clinical malaria in children under 5 years during the transmission season?
gold_reference_texts: SMC reduces clinical malaria risk in children < 5 years by almost 75% (risk ratio 0.27).

per_query.original_query: How did door-to-door delivery compare to fixed-point delivery for SMC coverage in Mali?
gold_reference_texts: In Mali, door-to-door SMC delivery achieved 76.1% coverage compared to 62.2% for fixed-point delivery.

per_query.original_query: What target age group has been evaluated in studies of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in school-aged children (IPTsc)?
gold_reference_texts: IPTsc has been evaluated in school-aged children between 5 and 15 years of age.

per_query.original_query: What precautions should be taken before administering IPTsc antimalarials to older girls of reproductive age?
gold_reference_texts: Girls of reproductive age must not be given certain IPTsc antimalarials without first confirming that they are not pregnant.

per_query.original_query: How is post-discharge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC) defined?
gold_reference_texts: PDMC is the administration of full antimalarial treatment courses at regular intervals after hospital discharge to children admitted with severe anaemia.

per_query.original_query: How did community-based delivery compare to facility-based delivery for adherence to PDMC?
gold_reference_texts: Community-based delivery of PDMC achieved 70.6% adherence compared to 52.0% for facility-based delivery.

per_query.original_query: By how much does PDMC reduce all-cause mortality during the intervention period in hospitalized children?
gold_reference_texts: PDMC reduces all-cause mortality during the intervention period with a risk ratio of 0.23.

per_query.original_query: What increase in QTc interval was associated with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHAP) administration during PDMC?
gold_reference_texts: DHAP was associated with an 18.6 ms mean increase in QTc interval following the third dose of each course.

per_query.original_query: What is mass drug administration (MDA) for malaria?
gold_reference_texts: MDA is the administration of full antimalarial therapeutic courses to all age groups in a defined population without prior testing.

per_query.original_query: What risk is associated with administering 8-aminoquinoline drugs during MDA for P. vivax in G6PD-deficient individuals?
gold_reference_texts: 8-aminoquinolines can cause severe haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals.

per_query.original_query: What is mass relapse prevention (MRP) for P. vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Mass relapse prevention (MRP) provides an 8-aminoquinoline drug to an entire population to clear P. vivax hypnozoites.

per_query.original_query: How long does the clinical incidence reduction effect of MDA typically last in moderate to high P. falciparum transmission settings?
gold_reference_texts: The clinical incidence reduction from MDA in moderate to high transmission settings wanes within 1 to 3 months.

per_query.original_query: Who should be excluded from receiving mass drug administration (MDA) antimalarial regimens?
gold_reference_texts: Exclusions for MDA include first-trimester pregnant women, infants under 6 months or under 5 kg, individuals recently treated with the same drug, allergic individuals, and severely ill persons.

per_query.original_query: What was the estimated cost per malaria case averted reported for MDA in emergency settings?
gold_reference_texts: One study estimated that MDA in an emergency setting cost US$ 46 per malaria case averted.

per_query.original_query: By what risk difference does MDA reduce P. falciparum prevalence 1–3 months post-MDA in low transmission settings?
gold_reference_texts: MDA reduces P. falciparum prevalence by a risk difference of -18 cases per 1000 persons at 1–3 months post-MDA in low transmission areas.

per_query.original_query: What rate of serious adverse events per 1000 doses was observed among participants in MDA trials?
gold_reference_texts: The rate of serious adverse events among MDA participants was 0.03 per 1000 antimalarial doses.

per_query.original_query: How did the cost per person reached for MDA compare between operational and research settings?
gold_reference_texts: The cost of MDA per person reached was US$ 2.90 in operational settings compared to US$ 4.71 in research settings.

per_query.original_query: What percentage of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections?
gold_reference_texts: 8% of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections.

per_query.original_query: What is the total dose of oral chloroquine recommended for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The total dose of oral chloroquine for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria is 25 mg base/kg body weight.

per_query.original_query: How is chloroquine dosed on the second day for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Chloroquine is given at 10 mg/kg body weight on the second day.

per_query.original_query: Which ACTs are recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: ACTs containing piperaquine, mefloquine or lumefantrine are recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria.

per_query.original_query: What is the risk ratio for recurrent parasitaemia with ACTs compared to chloroquine for P. vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: ACTs were at least as effective in preventing recurrent parasitaemia before day 28 with a risk ratio of 0.58 (95% CI, 0.18-1.90).

per_query.original_query: What G6PD activity threshold defines deficiency in qualitative near-patient tests?
gold_reference_texts: In males and females, <30% of normal G6PD activity is considered deficient.

per_query.original_query: What is the pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests?
gold_reference_texts: The pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests is 94.9% (95% CI 89.4, 97.6).

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended weekly primaquine dose for G6PD deficient patients?
gold_reference_texts: G6PD deficient patients should receive primaquine 0.75 mg/kg once a week for 8 weeks.

per_query.original_query: What is the dose of primaquine for patients with G6PD activity between 30 and 70%?
gold_reference_texts: Patients with intermediate G6PD deficiency between 30 and 70% should receive primaquine 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days or 7 days.

per_query.original_query: What is the sensitivity of the STANDARD G6PD test at the 70% threshold?
gold_reference_texts: The STANDARD G6PD test has a sensitivity of 91.4% (95% CI 75.5, 97.4) at the 70% threshold.

per_query.original_query: What is the total dose of tafenoquine recommended for adults weighing more than 35 kg?
gold_reference_texts: Adults and adolescents weighing more than 35 kg should receive a single 300 mg dose of tafenoquine.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended total primaquine dose for preventing relapse of P. vivax or P. ovale malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The total primaquine dose for preventing relapse is 7 mg/kg.

per_query.original_query: Which patient groups are excluded from primaquine treatment?
gold_reference_texts: Primaquine should not be given to pregnant women.
Primaquine should not be given to infants aged <1 month.
Primaquine should not be given to women breastfeeding infants aged <1 month.

per_query.original_query: What is the mortality rate of untreated severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Mortality from untreated severe malaria approaches 100%.

per_query.original_query: What is the mortality rate for severe malaria with prompt effective treatment?
gold_reference_texts: With prompt, effective treatment, the mortality rate for severe malaria falls to 10-20%.

per_query.original_query: What defines impaired consciousness in severe falciparum malaria in adults?
gold_reference_texts: Impaired consciousness in severe falciparum malaria in adults is a Glasgow coma score < 11.

per_query.original_query: What glucose level defines hypoglycemia in severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Hypoglycaemia in severe malaria is defined as blood or plasma glucose < 2.2 mmol/L.

per_query.original_query: What is the threshold for severe malarial anaemia in children under 12 years?
gold_reference_texts: Severe malarial anaemia in children under 12 years is defined as haemoglobin ≤ 5 g/dL or haematocrit ≤ 15%.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended parenteral antimalarial treatment for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Parenteral artesunate is the treatment of choice for all severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended duration of parenteral antimalarial treatment for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Parenteral antimalarial treatment should be given for at least 24 hours.

per_query.original_query: What is the initial dose of intramuscular artemether for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The initial dose of artemether is 3.2 mg/kg intramuscularly.

per_query.original_query: What is the maintenance dose of intramuscular artemether for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The maintenance dose of artemether is 1.6 mg/kg daily.

per_query.original_query: Which antimalarial drugs are not recommended as adjunctive treatments for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Heparin, prostacyclin, desferroxamine, pentoxifylline, low-molecular-mass dextran, urea, high-dose corticosteroids, aspirin, anti-TNF antibody, cyclosporine A, dichloroacetate, adrenaline, hyperimmune serum, N-acetylcysteine, and albumin bolus are not recommended for severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended parenteral antimalarial for pregnant women with severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Parenteral artesunate is the treatment of choice for pregnant women with severe malaria in all trimesters.

per_query.original_query: By what percentage does parenteral artesunate reduce mortality compared to quinine in adults with severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Parenteral artesunate reduced mortality by about 40% in adults with severe malaria compared to quinine.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended dose of parenteral artesunate for children weighing less than 20 kg with severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Children weighing < 20 kg should receive artesunate 3 mg/kg per dose.

per_query.original_query: What is the pre-referral treatment of choice for children under 6 years with suspected severe malaria when intramuscular artesunate is not available?
gold_reference_texts: Children < 6 years should receive rectal artesunate 10 mg/kg if intramuscular artesunate is not available.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended dose of rectal artesunate for pre-referral treatment in children?
gold_reference_texts: The dose of rectal artesunate is 10 mg/kg as a single dose.

per_query.original_query: What are the two general classes of poor-quality antimalarial medicines?
gold_reference_texts: The two general classes of poor-quality medicines are falsified and substandard medicines.

per_query.original_query: What is the treatment failure threshold that should trigger a change in national malaria treatment policy?
gold_reference_texts: A national malaria treatment policy should be changed if the treatment failure proportion is ≥ 10%.

per_query.original_query: What cure rate should a new antimalarial medicine have before being introduced into national treatment policy?
gold_reference_texts: A new antimalarial medicine should have a cure rate of > 95% before introduction.

per_query.original_query: What is mass testing and treatment (MTaT)?
gold_reference_texts: Mass testing and treatment (MTaT) involves testing the entire population of a geographical area and treating all positive cases.

per_query.original_query: Does mass testing and treatment reduce the prevalence of malaria two months after the last round?
gold_reference_texts: MTaT does not reduce malaria prevalence two months after the last round.

per_query.original_query: What is targeted drug administration (TDA)?
gold_reference_texts: Targeted drug administration (TDA) provides antimalarial medicine to individuals at increased risk of infection.

per_query.original_query: What is targeted testing and treatment (TTaT)?
gold_reference_texts: Targeted testing and treatment (TTaT) involves testing individuals at increased risk of malaria and treating positive cases.

per_query.original_query: What is reactive drug administration (RDA)?
gold_reference_texts: Reactive drug administration (RDA) provides antimalarial medicine to people living near a confirmed malaria case or those co-exposed with the index case.

per_query.original_query: What is reactive case detection and treatment (RACDT)?
gold_reference_texts: Reactive case detection and treatment (RACDT) involves testing people living near a confirmed malaria case or co-exposed with the index case and treating those who test positive.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended single dose of primaquine as a gametocytocide for uncomplicated falciparum malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The single dose of primaquine as a gametocytocide is 0.25 mg base/kg.

per_query.original_query: In which part of the world has artemisinin resistance in P. falciparum been documented?
gold_reference_texts: Artemisinin resistance in P. falciparum is present in parts of Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Thailand and Viet Nam.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended treatment for severe malaria in areas with established artemisinin resistance?
gold_reference_texts: Parenteral artesunate and parenteral quinine should be given together in full doses for severe malaria in areas with artemisinin resistance.

per_query.original_query: Which species of malaria are generally considered sensitive to chloroquine?
gold_reference_texts: P. ovale, P. malariae and P. knowlesi are considered sensitive to chloroquine.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended dose of chloroquine for uncomplicated malaria caused by P. ovale, P. malariae or P. knowlesi?
gold_reference_texts: P. ovale, P. malariae and P. knowlesi should be treated with the standard regimen of chloroquine or ACT.

per_query.original_query: What is the pooled sensitivity of semi-quantitative G6PD tests at the 30% threshold for the STANDARD G6PD test?
gold_reference_texts: The STANDARD G6PD test has a sensitivity of 100% at the 30% threshold.

per_query.original_query: In which region is tafenoquine recommended for preventing relapses of P. vivax?
gold_reference_texts: Tafenoquine is recommended for P. vivax relapse prevention in South America.

per_query.original_query: Which G6PD test is required before tafenoquine administration?
gold_reference_texts: Quantitative or semi-quantitative G6PD testing is required before tafenoquine.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended treatment for uncomplicated malaria when the species is not known with certainty?
gold_reference_texts: Uncomplicated malaria of unknown species should be treated as P. falciparum malaria.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended treatment for mixed malaria infections?
gold_reference_texts: ACTs are the treatment of choice for mixed malaria infections.

per_query.original_query: What is the prevalence of G6PD deficiency typically in tropical areas?
gold_reference_texts: G6PD deficiency prevalence in tropical areas is typically 3-35%.

per_query.original_query: What is the definition of hyperparasitaemia in severe P. falciparum malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Hyperparasitaemia in severe falciparum malaria is a parasite count > 10%.

per_query.original_query: What is the definition of hyperparasitaemia in severe P. knowlesi malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Hyperparasitaemia in severe knowlesi malaria is a parasite density > 100,000/µL.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended dose of quinine for severe malaria if the patient has persisting acute kidney injury after 48 hours?
gold_reference_texts: Quinine dose should be reduced to 10 mg salt/kg every 12 h in patients with persisting acute kidney injury after 48 hours.

per_query.original_query: What is the evidence quality for the recommendation that parenteral artesunate should be used for severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The recommendation for parenteral artesunate for severe malaria is based on high certainty evidence.

per_query.original_query: What was identified as a major driver of non-adherence to medicine during MDA implementation?
gold_reference_texts: Absenteeism was identified as one of the major driving forces of non-adherence to medicine during MDA.

per_query.original_query: Is MDA recommended to reduce P. falciparum transmission in moderate- to high-transmission settings?
gold_reference_texts: MDA to reduce P. falciparum transmission is not recommended in moderate- to high-transmission settings.

per_query.original_query: How are moderate- to high-transmission P. falciparum settings defined for the MDA recommendation?
gold_reference_texts: Moderate- to high-transmission settings are defined as P. falciparum prevalence greater than 10% or incidence above 250 cases per 1000 population per year.

per_query.original_query: What risk difference was reported for P. falciparum parasitaemia incidence 1–3 months after MDA in the cRCT?
gold_reference_texts: The cRCT reported a risk difference of -22 per 1000 person-years for P. falciparum parasitaemia incidence 1–3 months after MDA.

per_query.original_query: What was the rate of serious adverse events among people who participated in MDA?
gold_reference_texts: The serious adverse event rate among MDA participants was 0.01 per 1000 doses of antimalarial medicine.

per_query.original_query: How did reported acceptability of MDA change before and after the intervention in one study?
gold_reference_texts: One study reported that MDA acceptability increased from 62% before the intervention to 98% after.

per_query.original_query: How quickly does the transmission-reducing effect of MDA for P. vivax wane?
gold_reference_texts: The transmission-reducing effect of MDA for P. vivax wanes within 1–3 months.

per_query.original_query: How should antimalarial dosage be determined during MDA when possible?
gold_reference_texts: During MDA, drug dosage should be determined by weight wherever possible, using age only when weight is unknown.

per_query.original_query: Should MDA be given to people already receiving malaria chemoprevention such as SMC, PMC, or IPTp?
gold_reference_texts: MDA should not be given to individuals receiving other forms of malaria chemoprevention.

per_query.original_query: What risk difference in P. vivax prevalence was reported 1–3 months after MDA in five cRCTs?
gold_reference_texts: Five cRCTs reported a P. vivax prevalence risk difference of -113 per 1000 persons 1–3 months after MDA.

per_query.original_query: What adverse-event rate was reported among people who participated in MDA for P. vivax?
gold_reference_texts: The adverse-event rate among participants in P. vivax MDA was 19.9 per 1000 doses of antimalarial medicine.

per_query.original_query: Is mass treatment with an 8-aminoquinoline medicine alone recommended to reduce P. vivax transmission?
gold_reference_texts: Mass treatment with an 8-aminoquinoline medicine alone is not recommended to reduce P. vivax transmission.

per_query.original_query: Which two malaria vaccines are WHO-prequalified and recommended for use?
gold_reference_texts: RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M are WHO-prequalified and recommended malaria vaccines.

per_query.original_query: Which children are prioritized for WHO-recommended malaria vaccination?
gold_reference_texts: WHO recommends malaria vaccination for children in malaria-endemic areas, prioritizing moderate- and high-transmission areas.

per_query.original_query: What is the standard WHO-recommended malaria vaccine schedule for children?
gold_reference_texts: WHO recommends a four-dose malaria vaccine schedule for children from 5 months of age.

per_query.original_query: What is the minimum interval between malaria vaccine doses?
gold_reference_texts: The minimum interval between malaria vaccine doses is four weeks.

per_query.original_query: What is the volume of each R21/Matrix-M vaccine dose?
gold_reference_texts: Each R21/Matrix-M vaccine dose is 0.5 mL.

per_query.original_query: At what temperature should RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines be stored?
gold_reference_texts: RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines should be stored at 2–8 °C.

per_query.original_query: If the malaria vaccine used for a previous dose is unavailable or unknown, should the vaccination series be restarted?
gold_reference_texts: If a previous malaria vaccine product is unavailable or unknown, the series should be completed with an available WHO-recommended vaccine rather than restarted.

per_query.original_query: When is the small risk of febrile seizures after malaria vaccination most likely to occur?
gold_reference_texts: The small risk of febrile seizures occurs within seven days of malaria vaccination, mainly within 2–3 days.

per_query.original_query: By how much did three age-based doses of RTS,S/AS01 reduce clinical malaria during 12 months of follow-up in the Phase 3 trial?
gold_reference_texts: Three age-based doses of RTS,S/AS01 reduced clinical malaria by 51% during 12 months of follow-up in the Phase 3 trial.

per_query.original_query: By how much did age-based R21/Matrix-M vaccination reduce clinical malaria during 12 months after the third dose in the Phase 3 trial?
gold_reference_texts: Age-based R21/Matrix-M vaccination reduced clinical malaria by 66% during 12 months after the third dose in the Phase 3 trial.

per_query.original_query: What febrile-seizure rate was associated with R21/Matrix-M vaccination, and what was the outcome of those seizures?
gold_reference_texts: R21/Matrix-M was associated with about one febrile seizure per 2500 vaccinations, and all febrile seizures resolved without sequelae.

per_query.original_query: At an assumed R21/Matrix-M price of US$3 per dose, what median ICER per clinical case averted was predicted for a four-dose age-based schedule in perennial settings?
gold_reference_texts: At a vaccine price of US$3 per dose, the predicted median ICER for a four-dose age-based R21/Matrix-M schedule in perennial settings was US$7 per clinical case averted.

per_query.original_query: Did malaria vaccine uptake negatively affect other childhood vaccinations, ITN use, or care-seeking for febrile illness in the pilot introduction?
gold_reference_texts: Malaria vaccine uptake had no negative effect on other childhood vaccinations, ITN use, or health-seeking behaviour for febrile illness.

per_query.original_query: How did access to at least one malaria prevention tool change in Ghana after RTS,S/AS01 introduction?
gold_reference_texts: In Ghana, access to at least one malaria prevention tool increased from 61% to 94% after RTS,S/AS01 introduction.

per_query.original_query: About how many RTS,S/AS01 doses were administered across the three pilot countries, and how many children received a first dose?
gold_reference_texts: Across the three pilot countries, about 4.2 million RTS,S/AS01 doses were administered and more than 1.2 million children received a first dose.

per_query.original_query: What coverage levels did all three pilot countries reach for the first, third, and fourth RTS,S/AS01 doses?
gold_reference_texts: All three pilot countries reached more than 80% first-dose coverage, at least 69% third-dose coverage, and at least 40% fourth-dose coverage.

per_query.original_query: What reductions in all-cause mortality and hospitalization with severe malaria were observed after RTS,S/AS01 introduction in the pilot implementation?
gold_reference_texts: RTS,S/AS01 introduction was associated with a 13% reduction in all-cause mortality excluding injury and a 22% reduction in hospitalization with severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: Within what time after malaria symptom onset should programmes ensure access to diagnosis and effective treatment?
gold_reference_texts: Programmes should ensure access to early diagnosis and prompt effective treatment within 24–48 hours of malaria symptom onset.

per_query.original_query: How many effective antimalarial medicines with different mechanisms of action should be used to treat malaria episodes?
gold_reference_texts: All malaria episodes should be treated with at least two effective antimalarial medicines with different mechanisms of action.

per_query.original_query: At what temperature should malaria be suspected in a patient in a malaria-endemic area when there is no other obvious cause?
gold_reference_texts: In malaria-endemic areas, malaria should be suspected with a history of fever or temperature of at least 37.5 °C when there is no other obvious cause.

per_query.original_query: How quickly should parasitological diagnostic results be available after a patient presents with suspected malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Parasitological diagnostic results should be available within less than 2 hours of the patient presenting.

per_query.original_query: If the initial blood film is negative in a patient with manifestations compatible with severe malaria, how often should repeat blood films be examined?
gold_reference_texts: When the initial blood film is negative in a patient with manifestations compatible with severe malaria, repeat blood films should be examined at 6–12-hour intervals.

per_query.original_query: What is the approximate microscopy detection limit for malaria parasites under typical field conditions?
gold_reference_texts: Under typical field conditions, the sensitivity limit of light microscopy is approximately 100 malaria parasites per µL of blood.

per_query.original_query: What false-positive and invalid-rate thresholds does WHO use when selecting malaria RDTs?
gold_reference_texts: WHO malaria RDT selection criteria include a false-positive rate below 10% and an invalid rate below 5%.

per_query.original_query: What average sensitivity and specificity were reported for PfHRP2-detecting RDTs in symptomatic patients in endemic areas?
gold_reference_texts: PfHRP2-detecting RDTs had an average sensitivity of 95.0% and specificity of 95.2% in the systematic review.

per_query.original_query: How is uncomplicated malaria defined?
gold_reference_texts: Uncomplicated malaria is defined by malaria symptoms, a positive parasitological test, and no features of severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: When should antipyretics be used in young children with malaria, and what paracetamol dose is described?
gold_reference_texts: In young children with malaria, antipyretics should be used when core temperature is above 38.5 °C, and paracetamol may be given at 15 mg/kg body weight every 4 hours.

per_query.original_query: How many seizures within 24 hours should prompt treatment as severe malaria?
gold_reference_texts: Patients with more than two seizures within a 24-hour period should be treated as having severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: Which ACTs are recommended for children and adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria?
gold_reference_texts: The recommended ACT options are artemether-lumefantrine, artesunate-amodiaquine, artesunate-mefloquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and artesunate-pyronaridine.

per_query.original_query: Which patients should avoid artesunate-pyronaridine because of its association with liver transaminitis?
gold_reference_texts: Artesunate-pyronaridine should be avoided in individuals with known clinically apparent liver disease.

per_query.original_query: How many days of treatment with an artemisinin derivative should ACT regimens provide?
gold_reference_texts: ACT regimens should provide three days of treatment with an artemisinin derivative.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended artemether-lumefantrine dosing schedule?
gold_reference_texts: Artemether-lumefantrine is given twice daily for three days, for six doses total, with the first two doses ideally 8 hours apart.

per_query.original_query: What daily folic acid dose should not be given with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine because it significantly reduces SP efficacy?
gold_reference_texts: Folic acid at 5 mg daily significantly reduces SP efficacy and should not be given concomitantly.

per_query.original_query: What minimum daily doses of dihydroartemisinin and piperaquine are recommended for children weighing under 25 kg?
gold_reference_texts: Children weighing under 25 kg should receive at least 2.5 mg/kg/day dihydroartemisinin and 20 mg/kg/day piperaquine for three days.

per_query.original_query: Why should high-fat meals be avoided with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine?
gold_reference_texts: High-fat meals accelerate piperaquine absorption and increase the risk of potentially arrhythmogenic QT-interval prolongation.

per_query.original_query: In which patients should dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine not be used because of QT-prolongation risk?
gold_reference_texts: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine should not be used in patients with congenital QT prolongation or with conditions or medications that prolong the QT interval.

per_query.original_query: What are the two main causes of recurrent P. falciparum malaria described in the guideline?
gold_reference_texts: Recurrent P. falciparum malaria can result from re-infection or recrudescence.

per_query.original_query: What second-line treatment is recommended for P. falciparum treatment failure within 28 days?
gold_reference_texts: Treatment failure within 28 days should be treated with an alternative ACT known to be effective in the region.

per_query.original_query: How should presumed P. falciparum treatment failures occurring more than 4 weeks after initial treatment be managed operationally?
gold_reference_texts: Presumed treatment failures after four weeks should be considered new infections operationally and treated with the first-line ACT.

per_query.original_query: Why should mefloquine generally not be reused within 60 days of the first treatment?
gold_reference_texts: Reuse of mefloquine within 60 days is associated with increased neuropsychiatric reactions, so an alternative ACT should be used.

per_query.original_query: What primaquine regimen is recommended with an ACT to reduce P. falciparum transmission in low-transmission areas, and is G6PD testing required?
gold_reference_texts: In low-transmission areas, a single 0.25 mg/kg dose of primaquine should be given with an ACT to reduce P. falciparum transmission, and G6PD testing is not required.

per_query.original_query: What single primaquine dose is listed for patients weighing 25 to under 50 kg?
gold_reference_texts: Patients weighing 25 to under 50 kg are assigned a single primaquine dose of 7.5 mg base.

per_query.original_query: What effect did single primaquine doses above 0.4 mg/kg have on gametocyte carriage at day 8?
gold_reference_texts: Single primaquine doses above 0.4 mg/kg reduced gametocyte carriage at day 8 by around two thirds.

per_query.original_query: What was the prevalence of malaria infection in the first trimester in the cited Benin study?
gold_reference_texts: The cited Benin study reported a first-trimester malaria infection prevalence of 21.8%.

per_query.original_query: What treatment does the guideline recommend for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy?
gold_reference_texts: ACTs should be used to treat uncomplicated falciparum malaria in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy.

per_query.original_query: Which antimalarial drug classes are stated not to be used in pregnancy?
gold_reference_texts: Primaquine and tetracyclines should not be used in pregnancy.

per_query.original_query: What is the recommended treatment for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria during the first trimester of pregnancy?
gold_reference_texts: Pregnant women with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria should be treated with artemether-lumefantrine during the first trimester.

per_query.original_query: Are ACTs containing sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine recommended in the first trimester of pregnancy?
gold_reference_texts: ACTs containing sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine are contraindicated during the first trimester of pregnancy.

per_query.original_query: How did first-trimester artemether-lumefantrine compare with oral quinine for adverse pregnancy outcomes?
gold_reference_texts: First-trimester artemether-lumefantrine treatment was associated with a 42% lower risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than oral quinine.

per_query.original_query: Why should sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with artesunate be avoided in the first weeks of life?
gold_reference_texts: SP with artesunate should be avoided in the first weeks of life because SP can displace bilirubin and aggravate neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia.

per_query.original_query: How should infants weighing under 5 kg with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria be dosed with ACT?
gold_reference_texts: Infants weighing under 5 kg with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria should receive an ACT at the same mg/kg target dose as children weighing 5 kg.

per_query.original_query: How should non-immune travellers returning to non-endemic settings with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria be treated?
gold_reference_texts: Travellers with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria returning to non-endemic settings should be treated with an ACT.

per_query.original_query: What parasitaemia threshold defines uncomplicated hyperparasitaemia in the guideline?
gold_reference_texts: Uncomplicated hyperparasitaemia is defined as at least 4% parasitaemia without signs of severe malaria.

per_query.original_query: What total oral chloroquine dose is described as effective for chloroquine-sensitive P. vivax malaria?
gold_reference_texts: For chloroquine-sensitive P. vivax malaria, oral chloroquine at a total dose of 25 mg base/kg body weight is described as effective.
